decisions.evidence: Facilitated-diffusion transport step with no substrate-specific permease annotated in the genome; no gene names a (S)-propane-1,2-diol transporter.

No argA/argJ-type gene annotated: the only acetyl-related arginine-pathway genes are BT3395 'putative acetylglutamate kinase' (ArgB, different reaction) and BT3549/BT3758 acetylornithine deacetylase/aminotransferase; no N-acetylglutamate synthase annotation.

BT2076 'acetohydroxyacid synthase small subunit' and BT2077 'acetolactate synthase large subunit' are adjacent, co-oriented subunits of one obligate AHAS complex and are kept joined with AND; the alternative branch pairing BT2077 with BT0572 ('conserved hypothetical protein', no enzymatic annotation) is removed.

Same AHAS complex as ACHBS: BT2076 (small subunit) AND BT2077 (large subunit) are the annotated obligate subunit pair; the branch substituting the unannotated hypothetical protein BT0572 for the small subunit is removed.

BT0767 is annotated 'para-aminobenzoate synthase component I' (PabB), i.e. the preceding ADC synthase step rather than the ADC lyase, so no remaining alternative is annotated for this reaction; BT0431 is a conserved hypothetical protein with a conserved domain and could be the unannotated PabC.
BT0518 and BT3812 are both annotated as bifunctional AICAR transformylase/IMP cyclohydrolase (PurH) — same-name paralogs, which are not removed.

BT0530 'anthranilate phosphoribosyltransferase' (TrpD) is exactly this reaction; BT0531 'anthranilate synthase component II' and BT0532 'anthranilate synthase component I' are the subunits of anthranilate synthase, a different reaction and EC, so both are removed.

The AND-pair BT0741 'aspartate carbamoyltransferase regulatory chain' + BT0742 'aspartate carbamoyltransferase catalytic chain' (PyrI/PyrB) is exactly this reaction; the alternative BT0557 'carbamyl phosphate synthetase' is a different enzyme (it makes the carbamoyl phosphate substrate) and is removed.
BT1375 'aspartokinase' and BT2403 'aspartokinase/homoserine dehydrogenase' are both genuine aspartokinase annotations — same-name paralogs, which are not removed.
BT3184 is annotated 'L-aspartate oxidase' (NadB), exactly the enzyme of this reaction; it is the only such annotation in the genome.

All six alternatives are aminotransferases (four annotated 'aspartate aminotransferase', plus a generic aminotransferase and a pyruvate-dependent aminotransferase); aminotransferases are broad-specificity enzymes that the procedure does not remove.

BT3933 'chorismate mutase/prephenate dehydratase' and BT3934, whose annotation also names a chorismate mutase domain, are both compatible with chorismate -> prephenate; BT3936 is annotated solely 'prephenate dehydratase' (EC 4.2.1.51, the following reaction) and is removed.
BT3944 'putative chloride channel protein' and BT4650 'voltage-gated chloride channel protein' are both chloride transporters of the right substrate class, so neither is removed.

Non-specific outer-membrane diffusion step; both alternatives carry only broad structural annotations (OmpA-family outer membrane protein, putative MotB), so removing one would leave only a family-level annotation.
Non-specific outer-membrane diffusion step with the same two broadly annotated alternatives (OmpA-family outer membrane protein, putative MotB); no removal is justified.
Periplasm-to-cytoplasm Cu2+ permease step; no copper-specific permease is annotated (no copA/copper transporter entries), only generic transporter families.

BT0488 is annotated '2-dehydro-3-deoxygluconokinase' (exactly this reaction) but the alternative BT2799 is a 'PfkB family carbohydrate kinase', the very family that contains KdgK, i.e. a compatible family-level annotation that is not removed.
BT0895 and BT2814 are both annotated 'dihydrodipicolinate synthase' — same-name paralogs, which are not removed.

BT0892 'dihydroorotate dehydrogenase' and the immediately adjacent, co-oriented BT0891 'dihydroorotate dehydrogenase electron transfer subunit' are PyrD/PyrK, the NAD-dependent class 1B heterocomplex that performs exactly this NAD-linked reaction.
BT0250 'dihydroorotase (DHOase)' is exactly this reaction; the alternative BT0557 'carbamyl phosphate synthetase' is a different enzyme of the upstream step and is removed.

BT2058 'putative isoprenyl synthetase' and BT3261 'octaprenyl-diphosphate synthase' are both trans-prenyltransferases acting on the same substrate class; chain-length specificity cannot be decided from the annotation, so neither is removed.
No ketopantoate (2-dehydropantoate) reductase annotation in the genome; the only pantothenate-pathway hit is BT4308 'pantoate--beta-alanine ligase' (PanC, a later step).
No thymidylate (dTMP) kinase is annotated; BT2047 is thymidylate synthase (ThyA, a different reaction) and the other nucleotide kinases present are cytidylate/uridylate/adenylate kinases.
BT1403 and BT4099 are both annotated '1-deoxy-D-xylulose 5-phosphate synthase' — same-name paralogs, which are not removed.
BT1106 'fructose-bisphosphate aldolase class I' and BT1691 'fructose-bisphosphate aldolase' are same-name paralogs, and aldolases are explicitly protected from removal.

BT1275 'L-fuculose kinase' lies in the fucose operon with L-fucose isomerase, L-fuculose-1-phosphate aldolase and L-fucose permease; BT3763 is annotated 'rhamnulose kinase/L-fuculose kinase'. Both annotations name this enzyme, so they are given as alternatives.

No Fe3+-specific ABC import system is annotated (only outer-membrane 'putative ferric aerobactin receptor' BT0150 and family-level ABC transporter components), so only a family-level match is available.

BT3054 'succinate dehydrogenase flavoprotein subunit' and the adjacent, co-oriented BT3055 'succinate dehydrogenase iron-sulfur protein' form the succinate:quinone oxidoreductase complex that catalyses exactly this menaquinol/fumarate interconversion; the two catalytic subunits are joined as an obligate complex.
No galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase (galT) annotation exists; the only galactose-pathway hits are UDP-galactose 4-epimerase (BT2887) and sugar phosphomutases, which are different reactions.

BT3589 'glucose/galactose transporter' is the better match, but BT0436 'arabinose-proton symporter' is an MFS sugar/H+ symporter of the right substrate class and transporters of the right class are not removed.
BT0554 and BT3601 are both annotated 'glucosamine--fructose-6-phosphate aminotransferase' — same-name paralogs, which are not removed.
BT0785 'glutamine synthetase I' and BT4339 'glutamine synthetase' are same-name paralogs, which are not removed.
BT0555 and BT4582 are both annotated 'amidophosphoribosyltransferase' (PurF) — same-name paralogs, which are not removed.
Same two prenyltransferases as DMATT (BT2058 'putative isoprenyl synthetase', BT3261 'octaprenyl-diphosphate synthase'); both act on the same substrate class, so neither is removed.

BT3931 is annotated 'GTP cyclohydrolase I' (FolE), exactly this reaction; BT1564 is annotated '7-cyano-7-deazaguanine reductase' (QueF), a different enzyme and EC in the queuosine pathway, and is removed.
CO2 hydration is a genuinely spontaneous equilibration, and the alternative 'spontaneous' is not a gene; BT1681 'carbonic anhydrase' is correctly annotated for it, so the rule is left unchanged.

BT0203 (hisB, bifunctional imidazoleglycerol-phosphate dehydratase/histidinol phosphatase) and BT4257 'putative histidinol-phosphatase' both fit, and the third alternative BT2801 'inositol-1-monophosphatase' is a broad-specificity phosphatase, which the procedure protects from removal.

No homoserine kinase (thrB) is annotated; the homoserine-related genes present are O-acetylhomoserine (thiol)-lyase, homoserine O-succinyltransferase and the aspartokinase/homoserine dehydrogenase BT2403, all different reactions.
BT1858 and BT1861 are both annotated '2-isopropylmalate synthase' — same-name paralogs, which are not removed.

BT2074 is annotated 'ketol-acid reductoisomerase' (IlvC), exactly this enzyme, and sits in the branched-chain amino acid operon with acetohydroxyacid synthase subunits BT2076/BT2077 and dihydroxy-acid dehydratase BT2078.
Same enzyme as KARA1i: BT2074 'ketol-acid reductoisomerase' (IlvC) carries out the reductoisomerase step on 2-aceto-2-hydroxybutanoate as well, and is the only such annotation in the genome.

BT3767 'lactaldehyde reductase / L-1,2-propanediol oxidoreductase' is exactly this reaction, but the alternative BT0535 'iron-containing alcohol dehydrogenase' is a broad-specificity group III Fe-ADH of the same family as FucO and is not removed.
No lactose permease or beta-galactoside symporter is annotated in the genome; only family-level sugar transporters are present.

BT3300 'beta-glucosidase' and BT4714 'periplasmic beta-glucosidase, xylosidase/arabinosidase' are both beta-glucosidases of the right substrate class for laminaribiose hydrolysis, so neither is removed.
No laminaribiose- or beta-1,3-glucoside-specific ABC importer is annotated; only generic 'ABC transporter permease/ATP-binding protein' family annotations are available.

BT2881 and BT3923 are both annotated '2-C-methyl-D-erythritol 4-phosphate cytidylyltransferase' (same-name paralogs) and the third alternative BT1651 'pyrophosphorylase' is a family-level nucleotidyltransferase annotation, which is not removed.

No methylmalonyl-CoA decarboxylase annotation exists; BT2090/BT2091 are methylmalonyl-CoA mutase subunits (a different reaction) and the remaining hits are family-level biotin-carboxylase/carboxyltransferase subunits.

BT2011 'putative nicotinate-nucleotide adenylyltransferase' (NadD) is exactly this reaction; BT2815 'putative mutT family protein' is a Nudix pyrophosphohydrolase, a hydrolase of clearly different activity that cannot perform an adenylyl transfer, and is removed.
BT3717 is annotated 'ornithine carbamoyltransferase', matching the reaction's EC 2.1.3.3 exactly, and it is the only such gene; it lies next to the arginine/proline-pathway genes BT3718/BT3719.
The decarboxylation of 3-carboxy-4-methyl-2-oxopentanoate proceeds spontaneously after the LeuB oxidation step, and the 'spontaneous' alternative is not a gene; the rule is left unchanged.

The AND-pair BT1697 'pyruvate carboxylase subunit B' + BT1915 'pyruvate carboxylase subunit A' is exactly this reaction; BT1448 and BT1688 are 'biotin carboxyl carrier protein' subunits listed alone as alternatives to that complex (and sit in separate carboxylase operons), so both lone-subunit branches are removed.

No phosphoglucosamine mutase (glmM) annotation; BT1548 and BT3950 are 'phosphoglucomutase/phosphomannomutase', a family-level match of the alpha-D-phosphohexomutase superfamily on different substrates.
All four alternatives are broad-specificity aminotransferases (three 'aspartate aminotransferase', one generic 'aminotransferase'); redundancy is plausible and aminotransferases are not removed.
No specific 5-amino-6-(5'-phosphoribitylamino)uracil phosphatase is annotated; only generic haloacid-dehalogenase-like hydrolases/phosphatases, i.e. a family-level match.

BT_4366 is annotated 'pantothenate kinase' (CoaA), exactly this reaction; BT0184 'uridine kinase (uridine monophosphokinase)' is a pyrimidine nucleoside kinase of clearly different substrate class and EC, and is removed.

The only PLP-biosynthesis gene is BT3918 'pyridoxal phosphate biosynthetic protein pdxJ', which catalyses the DXP-dependent PNP synthase step, not EC 4.3.3.6; no pdxS/pdxT (Pdx1/Pdx2) genes are annotated.
No raffinose or alpha-galactoside proton symporter is annotated in the genome; only family-level sugar transporters are present.
BT2803, BT2804 and BT3576 are all annotated as ribokinases — same-name paralogs, which are not removed.
Outer-membrane diffusion step with no substrate-specific gene product; porin/diffusion reactions are left gene-less.
BT0346 'ribose 5-phosphate isomerase B' and BT1986 'putative ribose 5-phosphate isomerase' are same-name paralogs, which are not removed.

No tetrahydrodipicolinate succinylase (dapD) annotation; BT2085 'putative succinyl-diaminopimelate desuccinylase' is the downstream DapE reaction and BT0895/BT2814 are dihydrodipicolinate synthases, so only different reactions are annotated.

BT0652 'putative thiamine-phosphate pyrophosphorylase' (ThiE) is exactly this reaction; BT0790 'phosphomethylpyrimidine kinase' (ThiD) is a kinase of different EC that makes the HMP-PP substrate, and is removed.
BT3929 'triosephosphate isomerase' is exactly this reaction; BT1672 'phosphoglycerate kinase' is a different enzyme and EC acting on a different substrate, and is removed.

The rule mixes the catalyst BT4336 'thioredoxin reductase' with its thioredoxin substrates and with BT2811 'alkyl hydroperoxide reductase subunit F', a broad-specificity NAD(P)H flavoprotein disulfide reductase; collapsing it would require judgements the annotations do not settle, so the rule is left unchanged.
Same four broad-specificity aminotransferases as PHETA1; aminotransferases are not removed.

BT0623 'putative UDP-glucose 4-epimerase' fits exactly, but BT1370 'NAD dependent nucleotide-diphosphate-sugar epimerase' and BT0381 capD are sugar-nucleotide epimerase-family annotations compatible with the reaction, so neither is removed.

BT2242 'uridylate kinase' (PyrH) is exactly this reaction and BT2060 'cytidylate kinase' is a pyrimidine-nucleotide monophosphate kinase of compatible substrate class, so both are kept; BT4308 'pantoate--beta-alanine ligase' (PanC) is an unrelated ligase and is removed.
BT0792 'xylulose kinase (xylulokinase)' and BT4423 'xylulose kinase' are same-name paralogs, which are not removed.
